questions.question: 若い（　　）、いろいろな 国へ 行きたい。
questions.explanation: While you are still young: うちに.
questions.translation: While I'm still young, I want to go to lots of countries.
notes: たびに means "every time". Being young is one period, not something that repeats.
までに is a deadline (by a point in time). It can't follow an adjective like 若い.
ところで means "even if" or "by the way" here. "While I'm still young" is 若い うちに.

questions.question: 温かい（　　）、どうぞ めしあがって ください。
questions.explanation: While it's still warm: うちに. 前に cannot follow an adjective.
questions.translation: Please eat it while it's still warm.
notes: 前に follows a verb (冷める 前に), never an adjective. With 温かい, use うちに.
後で means "after", and it follows a た-form verb. "While it's still warm" is うちに.
ほどに shows degree (so … that). It doesn't mean "while". Use うちに.

questions.question: 昨日の 会議の（　　）、電話が 鳴った。
questions.explanation: N の 最中に = right in the middle of.
questions.translation: Right in the middle of yesterday's meeting, a phone rang.
notes: N の うちに means "before it changes / while it lasts" and is unnatural with one meeting. "Right in the middle of" is 最中に.
たびに means "every time". 昨日の 会議 is one meeting, so it can't repeat.
とたんに follows a た-form verb (始まった とたんに), not N の. Use 最中に.

questions.question: 食事を して いる（　　）に、客が 来た。
questions.explanation: 〜て いる 最中に.
questions.translation: Right in the middle of our meal, a guest came.
notes: とたん follows a た-form (した とたん), not 〜て いる. Use 最中.
たび follows a dictionary form (する たびに) and means "every time". It doesn't follow 〜て いる.
ばかりに means "just because (bad result)". A guest coming isn't caused by eating.

questions.question: ドアを（　　）とたん、猫が 飛び出した。
questions.explanation: た-form + とたん.
questions.translation: The moment I opened the door, the cat ran out.
notes: とたん follows the た-form. 開ける とたん is wrong; say 開けた とたん.
The て-form can't come before とたん. Use the た-form: 開けた.
The stem 開け doesn't connect to とたん. Use the た-form: 開けた.

questions.question: 立ち上がった（　　）、めまいが した。
questions.explanation: The moment I stood up: とたん.
questions.translation: The moment I stood up, I felt dizzy.
notes: 最中 needs 〜て いる or N の (会議の 最中). It can't follow a た-form.
うちに follows 〜て いる, 〜ない or an adjective, not a た-form. "The moment" is とたん.
たびに follows the dictionary form and means "every time". Standing up once is とたん.

questions.question: この 仕事が（　　）からでないと、帰れません。
questions.explanation: て-form + から でないと + negative.
questions.translation: I can't go home until this work is finished.
notes: からでないと needs the て-form: 終わって からでないと.
The た-form doesn't connect to から here. Use the て-form: 終わって.
The stem 終わり doesn't connect to から. Use the て-form: 終わって.

questions.question: ちゃんと 説明を（　　）からでないと、サインは できません。
questions.explanation: て-form + からでないと: not before you have heard it.
questions.translation: I can't sign until I've heard a proper explanation.
notes: からでないと needs the て-form: 聞いて からでないと.
The た-form doesn't connect to から here. Use the て-form: 聞いて.
The stem 聞き doesn't connect to から. Use the て-form: 聞いて.

questions.question: この 歌を 聞く（　　）、高校時代を 思い出す。
questions.explanation: Every time: dictionary form + たびに.
questions.translation: Every time I hear this song, I remember my high school days.
notes: ごとに follows a noun (一日ごとに, 会う 人ごとに). After a verb, "every time" is たびに.
とたんに follows the た-form and means "the moment". Every time you hear it is たびに.
最中に needs 〜て いる or N の. "Every time I hear" is 聞く たびに.

questions.question: ふるさとに 帰る（　　）、町が 変わって いて おどろく。
questions.explanation: Each time I go back: たびに.
questions.translation: Every time I go back to my hometown, I'm surprised at how much it has changed.
notes: うちに means "while (before it changes)". Going home happens many times, and each time you are surprised: たびに.
とたんに follows a た-form (帰った とたんに) and is one moment, not every visit.
最中に needs 〜て いる or N の. "Every time I go back" is 帰る たびに.

questions.question: 出かけようと した（　　）、電話が かかって きた。
questions.explanation: Something arrives just then: ところへ.
questions.translation: Just as I was about to go out, the phone rang.
notes: ところを comes before a verb that acts on you (〜ところを 見られた). With かかって きた, use ところへ.
ばかりに means "just because (bad result)". The phone didn't ring because you tried to go out.
うちに can't follow 〜ようと した. "Just as I was about to" is ところへ.

questions.question: 寝て いる（　　）、起こされた。
questions.explanation: ところを + passive (done to you at that moment).
questions.translation: I was woken up while I was sleeping.
notes: ところへ is for someone or something arriving (来た, かかって きた). 起こされた is done to you: ところを.
ところで here would mean "even if". With a passive done to you, use ところを.
うち takes に (うちに) and means "while it lasts". It never takes を.

questions.question: {物価|ぶっか}は 何年も 前から 上がる（　　）だ。
questions.explanation: Continuing change: dictionary form + 一方だ.
questions.translation: Prices have just kept going up for years.
notes: 上がる ところだ means "about to go up". 何年も 前から shows it has been rising for years: 一方だ.
はずだ is an expectation (should go up). It doesn't fit 何年も 前から. Keeps going: 一方だ.
つもりだ is a person's plan. Prices don't plan. Use 一方だ.

questions.question: 彼の 病気は 入院して から ずっと 悪く なる（　　）だ。
questions.explanation: Getting worse and worse: ばかりだ.
questions.translation: Since he went into hospital, his illness has just kept getting worse.
notes: なる ところだ means "about to get worse". ずっと shows it has kept getting worse: ばかりだ.
はずだ is an expectation, not a change that keeps going. Use ばかりだ.
うち needs に (うちに) and starts a clause. It can't end a sentence with だ.

questions.question: テーブルの 上に 食べ（　　）の パンが ある。
questions.explanation: Half-eaten: stem + かけ.
questions.translation: There's some half-eaten bread on the table.
notes: 食べ始め is "the start of eating", not "half-eaten". Half-eaten bread is 食べかけの パン.
食べ終わり is the end of eating. Bread you finished wouldn't be there. Half-eaten is 食べかけ.
すぎ means "too much" (食べすぎ). It doesn't describe bread. Use 食べかけ.

questions.question: 読み（　　）の 本が つくえに 3さつも ある。
questions.explanation: Half-read books: stem + かけ.
questions.translation: There are as many as three half-read books on my desk.
notes: A finished book is 読み終わった 本. 読み終わりの 本 isn't said, and it's the opposite of half-read.
すぎ means "too much" (読みすぎ). It doesn't describe a book. Half-read is 読みかけ.
がち is a habit (忘れがち). It doesn't describe a book. Half-read is 読みかけ.

questions.question: こんなに たくさんの 料理は 一人では 食べ（　　）。
questions.explanation: Can't finish it all: stem + きれない.
questions.translation: I can't eat this much food all by myself.
notes: 食べきる means "eat it all". 一人では shows you can't: 食べきれない.
かける means "start to / half-do". "Can't finish" is 食べきれない.
あう means "do to each other" (話しあう). It doesn't fit eating alone.

questions.question: 足が いたかったけど、マラソンを 最後まで 走り（　　）。
questions.explanation: To the end = きった.
questions.translation: My legs hurt, but I ran the marathon all the way to the end.
notes: けど sets up a contrast: legs hurt, BUT you still did it. 走りきれない (couldn't) is no contrast. Use 走りきった.
走りかけた means "started to run" or "half-ran". 最後まで needs 走りきった.
走り出した means "started running". 最後まで (to the end) needs 走りきった.

questions.question: 窓を 開け（　　）で 出かけて しまった。
questions.explanation: Left open: stem + っぱなし.
questions.translation: I went out and left the window open.
notes: 開けかけ means "half-opened". You left it open: 開けっぱなし.
きり means "only / since" (それきり). After a verb stem for "left as is", use っぱなし.
がち is a habit (忘れがち). "Left open" is 開けっぱなし.

questions.question: 電気を つけ（　　）に しないで ください。
questions.explanation: Left on: つけっぱなし.
questions.translation: Please don't leave the lights on.
notes: つけかけ means "half-done turning on". Leaving the light on is つけっぱなし.
がち is a habit, and it doesn't take に しないで. Use つけっぱなし.
気味 means "a bit of" ({風邪|かぜ}気味). Lights left on are つけっぱなし.

pattern: 〜ことに する / している
meaning: decide to / make it my rule

questions.pattern: 〜ことに する / している
questions.question: 私は {健康|けんこう}の ために、毎晩 10時に 寝る（　　）。(my own rule)
questions.correct: ことに して いる
wrong_options: ことに なって いる
ように なって いる
はずに なって いる
questions.explanation: Your own decision kept as a habit: ことに して いる.
questions.translation: For my health, I make it a rule to go to bed at 10 every night.
notes: ことに なって いる is a rule others made. (my own rule) means ことに して いる.
ように なって いる is a change that happened (now able to). Your own rule is ことに して いる.
はず can't take に なる. Your own rule is ことに して いる.

questions.pattern: 〜ことに する / している
questions.question: 迷ったけど、その 仕事は 断る（　　）。(I decided)
questions.explanation: Your own decision: ことに した. ことに なった = decided by others.
questions.translation: I hesitated, but I decided to turn that job down.
notes: ことに なった is decided by others or by events. (I decided) is ことに した.
ように なった is a gradual change (came to). A one-time decision is ことに した.
ことが あった means "there were times". The sentence is about one decision: ことに した.

pattern: 〜ことに なる / なっている
meaning: it has been decided / it's the rule

questions.pattern: 〜ことに なる / なっている
questions.question: 来月から 大阪の 支店で 働く（　　）。(the company decided)
questions.explanation: Decided by others: ことに なる.
questions.translation: It's been decided that I'll work at the Osaka branch from next month.
notes: ことに した is your own decision. The company decided: ことに なった.
ように した means "made an effort to". The company decided it: ことに なった.
ように なった is a gradual change (came to). It can't talk about next month. A decision: ことに なった.

questions.pattern: 〜ことに なる / なっている
questions.question: この {寮|りょう}では、夜 11時までに 帰る（　　）。(dormitory rule)
questions.correct: ことに なって いる
wrong_options: ことに して いる
ように して いる
questions.explanation: A rule: ことに なって いる.
questions.translation: In this dormitory, the rule is that you have to be back by 11 at night.
notes: ことに して いる is your own personal rule. A dormitory rule is ことに なって いる.
ように して いる means "I try to". The dormitory sets a rule: ことに なって いる.
ことが ある means "sometimes". A rule is ことに なって いる.

questions.question: 出かけ（　　）と した とき、雨が 降り出した。
questions.explanation: Volitional + と する = be about to.
questions.translation: Just as I was about to go out, it started to rain.
notes: と した after the dictionary form means "supposing". "About to" needs the volitional: 出かけよう と した.
The て-form doesn't connect to と する. Use the volitional: 出かけよう.
出かけない と した isn't "about to go out". Use the volitional: 出かけよう.

questions.question: 寝よう（　　）とき、友だちから 電話が あった。
questions.explanation: Volitional + と した とき = just as I was about to.
questions.translation: Just as I was about to go to sleep, I got a call from a friend.
notes: と して is a て-form. Before とき you need the た-form: 寝ようと した とき.
と なった is "it became". "Was about to" is volitional + と した.
に した means "decided on". After a volitional, use と した.

questions.question: 電気が ついて いる。彼は 家に いる（　　）。
questions.explanation: Strong conclusion: に 違いない.
questions.translation: The lights are on. He must be at home.
notes: はずが ない means "it can't be". The lights are on, so he must be home: に 違いない.
わけが ない means "no way". The light shows the opposite: に 違いない.
ことが ない means "never". It doesn't fit a guess. Use に 違いない.

questions.question: 彼の 顔が 赤い。お酒を 飲んだ（　　）。
questions.explanation: Strong guess from evidence: に 違いない.
questions.translation: His face is red. He must have been drinking.
notes: わけが ない means "no way". A red face suggests he did drink: に 違いない.
はずが ない means "can't be". The red face points the other way: に 違いない.
ことは ない means "no need". A guess from evidence is に 違いない.

questions.question: あんなに 勉強した 彼が 落ちる（　　）。
questions.explanation: Impossible: はずが ない.
questions.translation: There's no way he would fail after studying that hard.
notes: に 違いない means he must fail. After studying that hard, it's the opposite: はずが ない.
はずだ means he should fail. After studying so hard, it's はずが ない.
ことに なる means "it turns out / it is decided". A strong denial is はずが ない.

questions.question: かぎを かけたから、ドアが 開いて いる（　　）。
questions.explanation: I locked it, so it can't be open: はずが ない.
questions.translation: I locked it, so there's no way the door is open.
notes: に 違いない means "must be open". You locked it, so it can't be: はずが ない.
はずだ means "should be open". Locking it means the opposite: はずが ない.
わけだ means "no wonder". It needs a reason that leads to it. Locking leads to はずが ない.

questions.question: 彼は 本当に 男（　　）人だ。
questions.explanation: Has the qualities of: N らしい. 男みたい would mean "like a man" (when he isn't one).
questions.translation: He's a really manly man.
notes: みたい needs な before a noun (男みたいな 人), and that means someone like a man who isn't one. A manly man is 男らしい.
Noun + そうな is not a form. "Manly" is 男らしい.
ような needs の after a noun (男のような) and means "like a man", for someone who isn't one. Use らしい.

questions.question: たまには 学生（　　）勉強しなさい。
questions.explanation: Like a proper student, before a verb: らしく (adverb form).
questions.translation: Study like a proper student once in a while!
notes: らしい before a verb must be らしく (adverb form): 学生らしく 勉強しなさい.
みたいな comes before a noun. Before a verb it is みたいに, and it means "like (but not)". Use らしく.
ような needs の after a noun and comes before a noun. Before a verb: らしく.

questions.question: あの 雲は わたあめ（　　）だね。
questions.explanation: Resemblance (casual): N みたい. N よう needs の.
questions.translation: That cloud looks like cotton candy, doesn't it?
notes: N らしい is hearsay or "typical of". A cloud isn't cotton candy; it only looks like it: みたい.
Noun + そう is not a form. "Looks like" after a noun is みたい.
よう needs の after a noun: わたあめのようだ. As written, use みたい.

questions.question: まるで 夢（　　）話だ。
questions.explanation: Before a noun: みたいな. みたいに goes before a verb.
questions.translation: It's a story just like a dream.
notes: みたいに comes before a verb or adjective. Before 話 (a noun), use みたいな.
N らしい means "typical of N". A story isn't typical of a dream; it is like one: みたいな.
Noun + そうな is not a form. Before a noun, "like" is みたいな.

questions.question: この 服は 子ども（　　）。
questions.explanation: Childish: 子どもっぽい.
questions.translation: These clothes look childish.
notes: がち follows a verb stem or some nouns for a bad habit (病気がち). "Childish" is 子どもっぽい.
気味 means "a bit of" for a state ({風邪|かぜ}気味). Childish is 子どもっぽい.
子どもだらけ means "full of children". Clothes that look childish are 子どもっぽい.

questions.question: 彼は 忘れ（　　）から、メモを 渡して おこう。
questions.explanation: Tends to forget: 忘れっぽい.
questions.translation: He's forgetful, so let's give him a memo.
notes: らしい doesn't follow a verb stem. "Forgetful" is 忘れっぽい.
みたい doesn't follow a verb stem. "Forgetful" is 忘れっぽい.
ように doesn't follow a verb stem, and "forget-like" makes no sense. Use 忘れっぽい.

questions.question: 最近 疲れて いて、{風邪|かぜ}を ひき（　　）だ。
questions.explanation: Tend to catch colds: ひきがちだ.
questions.translation: I've been tired lately, so I tend to catch colds.
notes: っぽい follows a noun or adjective (子どもっぽい). With a verb stem for a bad habit, use がち.
だらけ follows a noun for "covered in" (どろだらけ). A habit is ひきがち.
やすい is already an adjective, so it can't take だ: ひきやすい (no だ). With だ, use がちだ.

questions.question: 冬は 外に 出ないから、運動不足に なり（　　）。
questions.explanation: Tends to happen (bad): stem + がち.
questions.translation: I don't go outside in winter, so I tend to not get enough exercise.
notes: っぽい follows a noun or adjective stem, not なり. A bad tendency after a verb stem is がちだ.
だらけ follows a noun for "covered in". A tendency is なりがちだ.
やすい is an adjective and never takes だ. Say なりやすい, or use がちだ.

questions.question: 今日は {風邪|かぜ}（　　）なので、早く 寝ます。
questions.explanation: A slight cold today: {風邪|かぜ}気味. {風邪|かぜ}がち = often catch colds.
questions.translation: I have a slight cold today, so I'm going to bed early.
notes: がち is a repeated habit (病気がち). Today's slight cold is {風邪|かぜ}気味.
{風邪|かぜ}だらけ would mean "covered in colds". A slight cold is {風邪|かぜ}気味.
{風邪|かぜ}ばかり means "only colds". It doesn't mean "a bit of a cold". Use 気味.

questions.question: プロジェクトは 予定より 少し 遅れ（　　）だ。
questions.explanation: A slight degree right now: 遅れ気味.
questions.translation: The project is running a little behind schedule.
notes: 遅れすぎ means "far too late", which clashes with 少し. A little behind is 遅れ気味.
だらけ follows a noun for "covered in" (間違いだらけ). It can't follow 遅れ here.
っぽい is "-ish / looks like" (子どもっぽい). Running a little behind is 遅れ気味.

questions.question: この 作文は 間違い（　　）で、先生の 赤い 字で いっぱいだ。
questions.explanation: Full of mistakes: 間違いだらけ.
questions.translation: This essay is full of mistakes and covered in the teacher's red corrections.
notes: 気味 means "a bit of" ({風邪|かぜ}気味). An essay covered in corrections is full of them: だらけ.
がち is a person's habit. An essay can't have a habit. Use だらけ.
っぽい can't take で like this; it becomes っぽくて, and means "seems". Full of mistakes is だらけ.

questions.question: 雨の 中 サッカーを して、服が どろ（　　）に なった。
questions.explanation: Covered in mud: どろだらけ.
questions.translation: We played soccer in the rain, and my clothes got covered in mud.
notes: 気味 is "a bit of" for a state ({風邪|かぜ}気味), not for mud. Covered in mud is どろだらけ.
がち is a habit after a verb stem. Covered in mud is どろだらけ.
どろっぽい means "mud-like", and before になった it would be どろっぽく. Covered in mud is だらけ.

questions.question: 彼は 知らない（　　）を した。
questions.explanation: Pretend not to know: 知らない ふりを する.
questions.translation: He pretended not to know.
notes: よう can't take を する. "Pretend" is 〜ふりを する.
そう can't take を する after 〜ない. "Pretend" is ふりを する.
まま is "as it is" (知らない まま). It can't take を する. Use ふり.

questions.question: 寝て いる（　　）を して、話を 聞いて いた。
questions.explanation: Pretend to be asleep: 寝て いる ふりを する.
questions.translation: I pretended to be asleep and listened to the conversation.
notes: まま means "as is" and doesn't take を して. Pretending is ふりを して.
よう can't take を して. Pretending to be asleep is 寝て いる ふり.
ところを して is not a phrase. Pretending is ふりを して.

questions.question: 彼は 留学生（　　）日本へ 来た。
questions.explanation: In the role of: として.
questions.translation: He came to Japan as an exchange student.
notes: にとって means "from the viewpoint of". Coming in the role of a student is として.
について means "about". "As an exchange student" is として.
によって means "by / depending on". A role is として.

questions.question: この 町は {温泉|おんせん}（　　）有名だ。
questions.explanation: Famous as: として 有名.
questions.translation: This town is famous for its hot springs.
notes: にとって means "for (someone)". Famous AS a hot spring town: として.
について means "about". Being famous as something is として.
に 対して means "toward / against". Being famous as something is として.

questions.question: 先生の 質問（　　）、だれも 答えなかった。
questions.explanation: Directed at: に 対して.
questions.translation: Nobody answered the teacher's question.
notes: に とって means "for (someone)". Answering toward a question is に 対して.
に よって means "by / depending on". "To the question" is に 対して.
と して means "as (a role)". Responding to a question is に 対して.

questions.question: 兄は スポーツが 好きなの（　　）、弟は 本が 好きだ。
questions.explanation: Contrasting two things: の に 対して.
questions.translation: My older brother likes sports, whereas my younger brother likes books.
notes: に とって means "for (someone)". A contrast between two people is に 対して.
に ついて means "about". "Whereas" is に 対して.
と して means "as (a role)". A contrast is に 対して.

questions.question: 国（　　）習慣が 違う。
questions.explanation: Varies depending on: に よって.
questions.translation: Customs differ from country to country.
notes: に とって means "for (someone)". "Differ from country to country" is に よって.
に ついて means "about". Variation by country is に よって.
と して means "as". Variation is に よって.

questions.question: この 絵は ピカソ（　　）かかれた。
questions.explanation: Passive agent (creator): に よって.
questions.translation: This picture was painted by Picasso.
notes: に とって means "for (someone)". The doer in a passive is に よって.
に ついて means "about". Who painted it in a passive is に よって.
に 対して means "toward". The doer of a passive is に よって.

questions.question: この 問題（　　）、質問が あります。
questions.explanation: About (formal): に 関して.
questions.translation: I have a question about this problem.
notes: に よって means "by / depending on". "A question about" is に 関して.
に とって means "for (someone)". A problem is not a person. "About" is に 関して.
と して means "as (a role)". "About this problem" is に 関して.

questions.question: {事故|じこ}の 原因（　　）、今 調べて います。
questions.explanation: Regarding the cause: に 関して.
questions.translation: We are now investigating the cause of the accident.
notes: に とって means "for (someone)". Investigating a topic is に 関して.
に 対して means "toward / in response to". Looking into a topic is に 関して.
に 加えて means "in addition to" and needs a second thing. Here it's "about the cause": に 関して.

questions.question: 東京（　　）、多くの 都市で イベントが ある。
questions.explanation: Including (main example first): を はじめ.
questions.translation: There are events in many cities, starting with Tokyo.
notes: に とって means "for (someone)". "Starting with Tokyo" in a list of cities is を はじめ.
に よって means "by / depending on". The first example in a group is を はじめ.
と して means "as". Tokyo as the first of many cities is を はじめ.

questions.question: 社長（　　）、社員 全員が パーティーに 参加した。
questions.explanation: Starting with the president: を はじめ.
questions.translation: Everyone in the company, starting with the president, took part in the party.
notes: に よって means "by". The president as the first of everyone is を はじめ.
に とって means "for (someone)". "Starting with the president" is を はじめ.
に 関して means "about". "Starting with" is を はじめ.

questions.question: この 祭りは 若者（　　）人気が ある。
questions.explanation: Mainly among: を 中心に.
questions.translation: This festival is popular mainly among young people.
notes: に よって means "by / depending on". Popular mainly among young people is を 中心に.
と して means "as". "Centered on young people" is を 中心に.
について means "about". "Mainly among" is を 中心に.

questions.question: 駅を（　　）、新しい 町が できた。
questions.explanation: A town built around the station: を 中心に.
questions.translation: A new town grew up around the station.
notes: を もとに means "based on (a source)". A town built around a place is を 中心に.
を はじめ means "starting with" in a list. A town around the station is を 中心に.
を 通して means "through". The town grew around the station: 中心に.

questions.question: この 映画は 事実（　　）作られた。
questions.explanation: Based on facts: を もとに.
questions.translation: This film was made based on a true story.
notes: に とって means "for (someone)". Made based on facts is を もとに.
を はじめ means "starting with". A film made from facts is を もとに.
に 対して means "toward". Based on facts is を もとに.

questions.question: アンケートの {結果|けっか}（　　）、新しい 商品を 開発した。
questions.explanation: Based on the survey: を もとに.
questions.translation: We developed a new product based on the results of the survey.
notes: を はじめ means "starting with" in a list. Built from results is を もとに.
に 対して means "toward / in response to". Using results as a base is を もとに.
に 加えて means "in addition to". The product was based on results: を もとに.

questions.question: 友だち（　　）彼女と 知り合った。
questions.explanation: Through a friend: を 通して.
questions.translation: I got to know her through a friend.
notes: に よって marks a doer or method, not a person who connects you. "Through a friend" is を 通して.
に 対して means "toward". Meeting her through a friend is を 通して.
に 関して means "about". Through a friend is を 通して.

questions.question: インターネット（　　）、世界の ニュースを 知る ことが できる。
questions.explanation: Through the internet: を 通して.
questions.translation: You can learn about news from around the world through the internet.
notes: に 対して means "toward". Learning news through the internet is を 通して.
を はじめ means "starting with" in a list. Through a medium is を 通して.
に 加えて means "in addition to". Through the internet is を 通して.

questions.question: 初めて 作った（　　）、とても おいしい。
questions.explanation: For a first try (better than expected): に しては.
questions.translation: For a first attempt, it's really delicious.
notes: と して means "as (a role)". "For a first try, it's good" is に しては.
に とって means "for (someone's view)". Better than expected is に しては.
に よって means "by / depending on". Better than expected is に しては.

questions.question: 初心者（　　）、ずいぶん うまいですね。
questions.explanation: Good for a beginner (better than expected): に しては.
questions.translation: You're quite good for a beginner.
notes: と して means "in the role of". Praise that is better than expected is に しては.
に よって means "by / depending on". "For a beginner" is に しては.
に とって is about someone's viewpoint. Better than expected for a beginner is に しては.

questions.question: 知らない（　　）、知って いる ふりを する。
questions.explanation: Criticism: くせに.
questions.translation: Even though he doesn't know, he acts like he does.
notes: おかげで is "thanks to" for a good result. Criticism with "even though" is くせに.
ために is "for / because". Acting like he knows doesn't happen for not knowing. Use くせに.
とおりに means "exactly as". The clash between not knowing and acting is くせに.

questions.question: 自分は 何も しない（　　）、人の {文句|もんく}ばかり 言う。
questions.explanation: Blame: does nothing, yet complains: くせに.
questions.translation: He does nothing himself, yet he's always complaining about other people.
notes: おかげで is "thanks to" a good result. Complaining isn't a good result. Criticism is くせに.
ために is "in order to / because". He doesn't complain in order to do nothing. Use くせに.
せいで blames a cause for a bad result. Doing nothing doesn't cause complaining; the two clash: くせに.

questions.question: 彼は よく 食べる（　　）、やせて いる。
questions.explanation: Not what you'd expect: わりに.
questions.translation: He eats a lot, but he's still thin.
notes: おかげで means "thanks to". Eating a lot doesn't make you thin. Use わりに.
ために means "because / in order to". Eating a lot isn't why he's thin. Use わりに.
ように means "so that / like". "Considering he eats a lot" is わりに.

questions.question: この レストランは 値段の（　　）、{量|りょう}が 多い。
questions.explanation: For the price (more than expected): N の わりに.
questions.translation: For the price, this restaurant gives you big portions.
notes: くせに is criticism of a person. Praise of a restaurant for its price is わりに.
せいで blames a bad result. Big portions are good: 値段の わりに.
うえに adds another point and follows a clause, not N の here. "For the price" is わりに.

questions.question: たとえ 雨が（　　）、試合は 行われる。
questions.explanation: たとえ always pairs with ても.
questions.translation: Even if it rains, the match will go ahead.
notes: たとえ always pairs with 〜ても. 降ったら is a normal "if".
たとえ pairs with 〜ても, not 〜ば.
たとえ pairs with 〜ても, not 〜と.

questions.question: たとえ みんなが（　　）、私は 彼を 信じる。
questions.explanation: たとえ always pairs with ても.
questions.translation: Even if everyone is against it, I believe in him.
notes: たとえ always pairs with 〜ても. 反対したら is a normal "if".
たとえ pairs with 〜ても, not 〜ば.
たとえ pairs with 〜ても, not なら.

questions.question: たくさん 練習した（　　）、負けて しまった。
questions.explanation: Despite: にも かかわらず.
questions.translation: Even though we practiced a lot, we lost.
notes: おかげで is "thanks to" a good result. Losing after practice is a surprise: にも かかわらず.
ために means "because". You didn't lose because you practiced. Use にも かかわらず.
とおりに means "exactly as". Losing despite practice is にも かかわらず.

questions.question: 注意した（　　）、彼は また 同じ ミスを した。
questions.explanation: Despite the warning: にも かかわらず.
questions.translation: Even though I warned him, he made the same mistake again.
notes: おかげで is "thanks to" a good result. Repeating a mistake is not one. Use にも かかわらず.
ために means "because". He didn't repeat it because you warned him. Use にも かかわらず.
うえに adds more in the same direction. Warning and repeating clash: にも かかわらず.

questions.question: 私が 英語を 教える（　　）、日本語を 教えて ください。
questions.explanation: In exchange: 代わりに.
questions.translation: I'll teach you English, and in return, please teach me Japanese.
notes: うえに adds one more thing. A swap (I teach, you teach back) is 代わりに.
わりに means "considering". An exchange is 代わりに.
くせに is criticism. An exchange is 代わりに.

questions.question: 今日は 母の（　　）、私が 晩ご飯を 作った。
questions.explanation: In place of my mother: の 代わりに.
questions.translation: Today I made dinner instead of my mother.
notes: わりに means "considering". Cooking in mother's place is 代わりに.
くせに criticizes someone. "Instead of my mother" is 代わりに.
せいで blames a cause. Cooking for her is 母の 代わりに.

questions.question: {寝坊|ねぼう}した（　　）、遅刻した。
questions.explanation: Bad result: せいで. おかげで is for good results.
questions.translation: I overslept, and because of that I was late.
notes: おかげで is "thanks to" a good result. Being late is bad: せいで.
くせに criticizes "even though". Oversleeping caused lateness: せいで.
わりに means "considering". A cause with a bad result is せいで.

questions.question: {先輩|せんぱい}が 教えて くれた（　　）、試験に 合格できた。
questions.explanation: Good result, with thanks: おかげで.
questions.translation: Thanks to my senior teaching me, I passed the exam.
notes: せいで blames a bad result. Passing is good: おかげで.
くせに is criticism "even though". Thanks for help is おかげで.
わりに means "considering". A helpful cause is おかげで.

questions.question: {事故|じこ}の（　　）、電車が 遅れて います。
questions.explanation: Formal cause: N の ため. せい / おかげ need で.
questions.translation: Because of an accident, the trains are running late.
notes: せい needs で to link the clause: {事故|じこ}の せいで. Alone it doesn't connect. Formal "because of" is ため.
おかげ is for good results, and needs で. Trains running late is not good: ため.
わけ means "reason / no wonder", not "because of". Use ため.

questions.question: 大雪の（　　）、飛行機が {欠航|けっこう}に なった。
questions.explanation: Formal cause: N の ため. せい / おかげ would need で.
questions.translation: Because of heavy snow, the flight was cancelled.
notes: せい needs で: 大雪の せいで. Alone it doesn't connect. Formal "because of" is ため.
おかげ is for good results, and needs で. A cancelled flight is not good: ため.
わけ means "reason / no wonder". A formal cause is ため.

questions.question: あなたを 信じて いる（　　）、本当の ことを 話すのです。
questions.explanation: Emphasized reason: からこそ.
questions.translation: It's precisely because I believe in you that I'm telling you the truth.
notes: ものの means "although". Believing you and telling the truth don't clash. Use からこそ.
ばかりに is "just because" for a bad result. Telling the truth here is not bad: からこそ.
のに is "even though". Belief and honesty go together: からこそ.

questions.question: 失敗した（　　）、わかる ことも ある。
questions.explanation: Precisely because you failed: からこそ.
questions.translation: There are things you only understand precisely because you failed.
notes: からには means "now that (so I must)". It needs a resolve after it. "Precisely because" is からこそ.
くせに is criticism "even though". Learning from failure is からこそ.
わりに means "considering". "Precisely because I failed" is からこそ.

questions.question: うそを ついた（　　）、信用を なくした。
questions.explanation: Only because of that, something bad happened: ばかりに.
questions.translation: Just because I told a lie, I lost people's trust.
notes: からこそ stresses a good or right reason. A lie causing a loss is ばかりに.
おかげで is "thanks to" a good result. Losing trust is bad: ばかりに.
うちに means "while". One lie that caused a loss is ばかりに.

questions.question: 会議で 余計な ことを 言った（　　）、部長に 怒られた。
questions.explanation: Just because of that one thing, a bad result: ばかりに.
questions.translation: Just because I said something unnecessary at the meeting, I got scolded by the department manager.
notes: からこそ stresses a good or right reason. A regretted cause is ばかりに.
おかげで is "thanks to" a good result. Being scolded is bad: ばかりに.
くせに criticizes "even though". "Just because I said it" is ばかりに.

questions.question: 彼は 10年 アメリカに 住んで いた。英語が 上手な（　　）だ。
questions.explanation: No wonder: わけだ.
questions.translation: He lived in America for 10 years. No wonder his English is good.
notes: ためだ gives a cause: "it's because his English is good". The 10 years are the cause, so "no wonder" is わけだ.
ことだ gives advice or feeling. "No wonder" is わけだ.
ところだ is about timing (about to / just did). "No wonder" is わけだ.

questions.question: 窓が 開いて いる。どうりで 寒い（　　）。
questions.explanation: No wonder (どうりで … わけだ).
questions.translation: The window is open. No wonder it's cold.
notes: はずが ない means "can't be". It is cold, and the open window explains it: わけだ.
ことだ gives advice. "No wonder" is わけだ.
ものか is "as if!" (strong denial). The open window explains the cold: わけだ.

questions.question: 肉が きらいな（　　）が、あまり 食べない。
questions.explanation: Partial denial: わけでは ない.
questions.translation: It's not that I dislike meat, but I don't eat it much.
notes: わけが ない means "there's no way". Partial denial (it's not that) is わけでは ない.
はずが ない means "can't be". "It's not that I dislike it" is わけでは ない.
わけだ means "no wonder / that's why". Before が (but), "it's not that" is わけでは ない.

questions.question: 料理が できない（　　）。面倒なだけだ。
wrong_options: わけには いかない
questions.explanation: It's not that I can't: わけでは ない.
questions.translation: It's not that I can't cook. It's just a hassle.
notes: ことだ gives advice ("you should"). "It's not that I can't" is わけでは ない.
わけだ means "no wonder". The next sentence says it's only a hassle: わけでは ない.
わけには いかない means "I can't (for a reason)". "It's not that I can't cook" is わけでは ない.

questions.question: 明日は 試験だから、遊びに 行く（　　）。
questions.correct: わけには いかない
questions.explanation: Socially or morally can't: わけには いかない.
questions.translation: I have an exam tomorrow, so I can't go out to have fun.
notes: わけでは ない means "it's not that". "I can't (because of the exam)" is わけには いかない.
はずが ない is a guess about something. Your own choice not to go is わけには いかない.
ことは ない means "no need". The exam stops you: わけには いかない.

questions.question: お客さんが 待って いるので、ここで 休む（　　）。
questions.correct: わけには いかない
questions.explanation: Can't, given the situation: わけには いかない.
questions.translation: Customers are waiting, so I can't take a break here.
notes: わけでは ない means "it's not that". You can't rest for a reason: わけには いかない.
わけが ない is "no way (it's true)". You can't rest because of a reason: わけには いかない.
わけだ means "no wonder". "I can't take a break" is わけには いかない.

questions.question: こんな 難しい 問題、子どもに わかる（　　）。
wrong_options: わけには いかない
questions.explanation: Impossible: わけが ない.
questions.translation: There's no way a child could understand such a difficult problem.
notes: わけでは ない means "it's not that". "There's no way" is わけが ない.
わけには いかない means "I can't (for a reason)". A child understanding is impossible: わけが ない.
ことに なる means "it turns out / it's decided". "No way" is わけが ない.

questions.question: あの まじめな 人が うそを つく（　　）。
wrong_options: わけには いかない
questions.explanation: No way: わけが ない.
questions.translation: There's no way that serious person would tell a lie.
notes: わけでは ない means "it's not that". A strong denial is わけが ない.
わけだ means "no wonder". He wouldn't lie: わけが ない.
わけには いかない means "I can't (for a reason)". About someone else's act, "no way" is わけが ない.

questions.question: 時間（　　）あれば、手伝いますよ。
questions.explanation: The one condition needed: さえ … ば.
questions.translation: As long as I have time, I'll help you.
notes: こそ means "precisely this". "As long as I have time" is さえ 〜ば.
しか needs a negative (時間しか ない). With あれば, use さえ.
まで means "even / until". The condition "as long as" is さえ.

questions.question: この 薬を 飲み（　　）すれば、すぐ 治りますよ。
questions.explanation: Just take it and you'll be fine: stem + さえ すれば.
questions.translation: As long as you take this medicine, you'll get better soon.
notes: こそ means "precisely". "As long as you take it" is stem + さえ すれば.
しか needs a negative. With すれば, use さえ.
だけ doesn't go between the stem and すれば. "As long as" is 飲みさえ すれば.

questions.question: もし {宝|たから}くじが 当たった（　　）、何を 買いますか。
questions.explanation: Hypothesis: としたら.
questions.translation: If you won the lottery, what would you buy?
notes: ところで means "even if (it's no use)". A real "if" asking what you'd buy is としたら.
うえで means "after / in doing". A supposition is としたら.
ばかりに is "just because" for a bad result. A supposition is としたら.

questions.question: もし 1か月 休みが ある（　　）、どこへ 行きたいですか。
questions.explanation: Supposing: としたら.
questions.translation: If you had a month off, where would you want to go?
notes: ところで means "even if (no use)". "If you had" is としたら.
わりに means "considering". A supposition is としたら.
くせに criticizes "even though". A supposition is としたら.

questions.question: もっと 早く（　　）、間に合ったのに。
questions.explanation: Regret: ば … のに.
questions.translation: If I had left earlier, I would have made it in time.
notes: と is for a result that always or then naturally follows. Regret about the past is 〜ば 〜たのに.
ても means "even if". Leaving earlier would have helped: 出れば.
なら is "if that's the case" about a topic. Regret about the past is 出れば.

questions.question: もっと 勉強（　　）、合格できたのに。
questions.explanation: Regret: すれば … のに.
questions.translation: If I had studied more, I could have passed.
notes: と is for a natural result, not past regret. Use すれば 〜たのに.
しても means "even if". More study would have helped: すれば.
するなら is "if you are going to". Past regret is すれば.

questions.question: 危なく 車に ひかれる（　　）。
questions.explanation: Nearly happened: ところだった.
questions.translation: I was nearly hit by a car.
notes: はずだった is a plan or expectation that didn't happen. "Nearly" is ところだった.
つもりだった is your own plan. Nobody plans to be hit. Use ところだった.
ことだった doesn't mean "nearly". Use ところだった.

questions.question: 目覚ましが 鳴らなかったら、{寝坊|ねぼう}する（　　）。
questions.explanation: Nearly happened: ところだった.
questions.translation: If my alarm hadn't gone off, I would have overslept.
notes: はずだった is an expectation, not a near miss. "Would have overslept" is ところだった.
つもりだった is your own plan. Oversleeping isn't planned: ところだった.
ばかりだった means "had just". A near miss is ところだった.

questions.question: 忙しくて、ご飯を 食べる 時間（　　）ない。
questions.explanation: Not even: さえ + negative.
questions.translation: I'm so busy I don't even have time to eat.
notes: こそ means "precisely". "Not even time to eat" is さえ + negative.
ばかり means "only / just", and ばかり ない is not natural. "Not even" is さえ.
だけ ない would mean "only the time to eat is missing". "Not even" is さえ.

questions.question: こんな {簡単|かんたん}な 漢字（　　）書けないの？
questions.explanation: Not even this easy kanji: さえ + negative.
questions.translation: You can't even write such an easy kanji?
notes: こそ is "precisely this" for emphasis. "Not even this easy kanji" is さえ + negative.
ほど is degree (not as … as). "Not even" is さえ.
ばかり means "only / nothing but". "Can't write even this" is さえ.

questions.question: 今年（　　）試験に 合格するぞ。
questions.explanation: Emphasis: こそ.
questions.translation: This year, I'm definitely going to pass the exam!
notes: さえ means "even". "This year for sure" is こそ.
しか needs a negative. "This year, definitely" is こそ.
だけ means "only this year". A strong resolve is こそ.

questions.question: こちら（　　）、よろしく お願いします。
questions.explanation: Set phrase: こちらこそ.
questions.translation: Likewise — I look forward to working with you too.
notes: さえ means "even". The set reply "likewise" is こちらこそ.
だけ means "only". The set reply is こちらこそ.
しか needs a negative. The set reply is こちらこそ.

questions.question: おばけ（　　）いる わけが ない。
questions.explanation: Dismissive: なんて.
questions.translation: There's no way ghosts exist.
notes: こそ stresses something as the real one. Dismissing ghosts is なんて.
さえ means "even". Looking down on an idea is なんて.
だけ means "only". "Things like ghosts" is なんて.

questions.question: あの 人が 犯人だ（　　）、信じられない。
questions.explanation: Surprise or disbelief: だ なんて.
questions.translation: I can't believe that person is the culprit.
notes: こそ stresses something. Surprise or disbelief is なんて.
さえ means "even". "To think that he is the culprit" is なんて.
ばかり means "only". Disbelief is なんて.

questions.question: 彼は 英語（　　）、フランス語も 話せる。
questions.explanation: Not only … but also: だけでなく … も.
questions.translation: He can speak not only English but also French.
notes: しか needs a negative, and も doesn't follow. "Not only … but also" is だけでなく.
だけに means "precisely because". "Not only" is だけでなく.
ばかりに is "just because" for a bad result. "Not only" is だけでなく.

questions.question: あの 先生は 学生（　　）、ほかの 先生からも {尊敬|そんけい}されて いる。
questions.explanation: Not only students: だけでなく … も.
questions.translation: That teacher is respected not only by students but also by other teachers.
notes: しか needs a negative. "Not only students" is だけでなく.
だけに means "precisely because". "Not only" is だけでなく.
ばかりに is "just because" for a bad result. Use だけでなく.

questions.question: 遊んで（　　）いないで、勉強しなさい。
questions.explanation: Only ever doing: て ばかり いる.
questions.translation: Stop just playing around and study!
notes: 〜て だけ いる isn't said. "Doing nothing but" is 〜て ばかり いる.
しか needs a negative verb (しか ない). "Only playing" is 遊んで ばかり.
こそ stresses a reason or thing. "Nothing but playing" is 遊んで ばかり.

questions.question: 息子は 毎日 ゲームを し（　　）いる。
questions.explanation: Does nothing but play: て ばかり いる.
questions.translation: My son does nothing but play games every day.
notes: 〜て しか needs a negative. "Does nothing but" is 〜て ばかり いる.
〜て だけ いる isn't a pattern. Use 〜て ばかり いる.
〜て こそ means "only by doing". "Nothing but games" is 〜て ばかり.

questions.question: 雨（　　）風も 強く なって きた。
questions.explanation: In addition: に 加えて.
questions.translation: On top of the rain, the wind has gotten stronger too.
notes: に よって means "by / because of". Rain plus wind is に 加えて.
に 対して means "toward / whereas". Adding another thing is に 加えて.
に とって means "for (someone)". "On top of the rain" is に 加えて.

questions.question: 給料（　　）、ボーナスも もらった。
questions.explanation: On top of the salary: に 加えて.
questions.translation: On top of my salary, I also got a bonus.
notes: に 対して means "toward / whereas". Salary plus bonus is に 加えて.
に とって means "for (someone)". Adding is に 加えて.
を 通して means "through". "On top of my salary" is に 加えて.

questions.question: この 店は 安い（　　）、おいしい。
questions.explanation: Adding a plus: うえに.
questions.translation: This shop is cheap, and on top of that, the food is good.
notes: くせに criticizes "even though". Two good points together is うえに.
ために means "because / for". Being cheap doesn't make food good: うえに.
ばかりに is "just because" with a bad result. Two good points: うえに.

questions.question: 今日は 寒い（　　）、雨も 降って いる。
questions.explanation: Cold, and on top of that, rain: うえに.
questions.translation: It's cold today, and on top of that, it's raining.
notes: くせに criticizes a person. Two bad points about weather is うえに.
わりに means "considering", for a surprise. Cold plus rain adds up: うえに.
ばかりに is "just because" with a result. Adding is うえに.

questions.question: 買い物（　　）、{郵便局|ゆうびんきょく}に 寄った。
questions.explanation: Doing it on the way: ついでに.
questions.translation: While I was out shopping, I stopped by the post office.
notes: の 代わりに means "instead of". You did both: の ついでに.
の わりに means "considering". "While out shopping" is の ついでに.
の くせに criticizes. "While I was at it" is の ついでに.

questions.question: 散歩の（　　）、パンを 買って きた。
questions.explanation: While out walking: の ついでに.
questions.translation: While I was out for a walk, I bought some bread.
notes: 代わりに means "instead of". You walked and also bought bread: ついでに.
わりに means "considering". "While I was out" is ついでに.
くせに criticizes. "While I was out" is ついでに.

questions.question: 上手に なりたければ、毎日 練習する（　　）。
questions.explanation: Advice: dictionary form + ことだ.
questions.translation: If you want to get good, you should practice every day.
notes: わけだ means "no wonder". Advice is ことだ.
はずだ is an expectation. Advice "you should" is ことだ.
ところだ is about timing. Advice is ことだ.

questions.question: やせたいなら、あまい ものを 食べない（　　）。
questions.explanation: Advice: ない-form + ことだ.
questions.translation: If you want to lose weight, you should stop eating sweet things.
notes: わけだ means "no wonder". Advice is ことだ.
はずだ is an expectation. Advice is ことだ.
ところだ is about timing (about to). Advice is ことだ.

questions.question: {簡単|かんたん}な 試験だから、そんなに 心配する（　　）よ。
questions.explanation: No need: ことは ない.
questions.translation: It's an easy exam, so there's no need to worry so much.
notes: ことだ is advice: "you should worry". An easy exam means no need: ことは ない.
わけだ means "no wonder". An easy exam doesn't explain worrying. Use ことは ない.
ことが ある means "sometimes". "No need to worry" is ことは ない.

questions.question: すぐ 治る けがだから、病院へ 行く（　　）よ。
questions.explanation: No need to go: ことは ない.
questions.translation: It's an injury that will heal quickly, so there's no need to go to the hospital.
notes: わけだ means "no wonder". "No need to go" is ことは ない.
はずだ is an expectation. "No need" is ことは ない.
ものだ is "one should / that's how it is". It says the opposite. "No need" is ことは ない.

questions.question: 約束は 守る（　　）だ。
questions.explanation: Moral should: べきだ.
questions.translation: You should keep your promises.
notes: べく means "in order to" and can't end a sentence with だ. "You should" is べきだ.
わけだ means "that's why". There's no reason before it. "Should" is べきだ.
ためだ means "it's for / because of". A rule of what to do is べきだ.

questions.question: 人の 悪口を 言う（　　）ではない。
questions.explanation: Should not: べきでは ない.
questions.translation: You shouldn't speak badly of other people.
notes: はずでは ない isn't the pattern: "can't be" is はずが ない. "Shouldn't" is べきでは ない.
ようでは ない is not "shouldn't". Use べきでは ない.
ためでは ない means "not for the purpose of". "Shouldn't" is べきでは ない.

questions.question: 子どもの ころは、よく この 川で 遊んだ（　　）だ。
questions.explanation: Nostalgia: た-form + ものだ.
questions.translation: When I was a child, I used to play in this river a lot.
notes: ことだ gives advice. Remembering a past habit is ものだ.
た ところだ means "have just done". 子どもの ころ is long ago: ものだ.
わけだ means "no wonder". Nostalgia is た-form + ものだ.

questions.question: 学生の ころは、よく 夜 遅くまで 友だちと 話した（　　）。
questions.explanation: Nostalgia: た-form + ものだ.
questions.translation: When I was a student, I would often talk with my friends until late at night.
notes: ことだ gives advice. A fond past habit is ものだ.
た ばかりだ means "have just done". 学生の ころ is long ago: ものだ.
わけだ means "no wonder". Nostalgia is た-form + ものだ.

questions.question: 私は 彼に もっと 早く 帰って（　　）。
questions.explanation: Want someone else to do: て ほしい.
questions.translation: I want him to come home earlier.
notes: たい is for your own action. Wanting someone else to do it is 〜て ほしい.
くれる has the other person as the subject (彼が 帰って くれる). With 私は 彼に, use ほしい.
ほしがる is for a third person's wish. Your own wish is ほしい.

questions.question: 部屋が 寒いので、窓を 閉めて（　　）んですが。
questions.explanation: Wanting someone else to do it: て ほしい.
questions.translation: The room is cold, so I'd like you to close the window.
notes: 〜て たい is not a form, and たい is for your own action. Asking someone is 〜て ほしい.
ほしがる describes a third person's wish. Your own request is ほしい.
くれる can't take たい. Asking someone is 閉めて ほしい.

questions.question: では、発表を 始め（　　）いただきます。
questions.explanation: Humble "let me": させて いただく.
questions.translation: Well then, allow me to begin my presentation.
notes: られて is passive. "Let me begin" is causative: 始めさせて いただきます.
させられて is "be made to". Asking permission is させて いただく.
せて is not a form for 始める (an る-verb). Its causative is 始めさせて.

questions.question: では、お先に 失礼（　　）いただきます。
questions.explanation: Set humble phrase: 失礼させて いただきます.
questions.translation: Well then, if you'll excuse me, I'll be leaving first.
notes: されて is passive. The set phrase is 失礼させて いただきます.
させられて is "be made to". The set phrase uses させて.
せて is not a form of する. Its causative is させて: 失礼させて.

questions.question: 先生は 学生に 宿題を 忘れない（　　）言った。
questions.explanation: Indirect request: ように 言う.
questions.translation: The teacher told the students not to forget their homework.
notes: ために is a purpose. Reporting an order is 〜ない ように 言う.
ことを 言った reports content, not an order. Use ように.
そうに means "looking like". A reported request is ように.

questions.question: 医者に お酒を 飲まない（　　）言われた。
questions.explanation: Told not to drink: ない-form + ように 言われた.
questions.translation: I was told by the doctor not to drink alcohol.
notes: ために is a purpose. A reported order is 〜ない ように 言われた.
ことを 言われた reports content, not an order. Use ように.
そうに means "looking like". A reported request is ように.

questions.question: のどが かわいて（　　）。
questions.explanation: Can't stand it: て たまらない.
questions.translation: I'm terribly thirsty.
notes: いられない comes after 〜ずには (can't help doing). After an adjective て, "unbearably" is たまらない.
すまない means "sorry". "Terribly thirsty" is かわいて たまらない.
かまわない means "it's fine" and needs も (〜ても かまわない). Use たまらない.

questions.question: 明日 彼女に 会えると 思うと、うれしくて（　　）。
questions.explanation: So happy I can't stand it: て たまらない.
questions.translation: When I think that I'll see her tomorrow, I'm so happy I can't stand it.
notes: いられない comes after 〜ずには. After うれしくて, "unbearably" is たまらない.
かまわない means "it's fine" and needs も. Use たまらない.
すまない means "sorry". "So happy" is うれしくて たまらない.

questions.question: 会議は 何時からだった（　　）。
questions.explanation: Trying to remember: っけ.
questions.translation: What time did the meeting start again?
notes: ぞ is a strong statement. Trying to remember is っけ.
わ is a soft statement. With 何時, you are asking: っけ.
よ tells new information. You are trying to remember: っけ.

questions.question: あの 人の 名前、何だった（　　）。
questions.explanation: Trying to remember: だった っけ.
questions.translation: What was that person's name again?
notes: ぞ is a strong statement. Trying to remember is っけ.
さ is a casual statement. Asking yourself again is っけ.
わ is a soft statement. Trying to remember is っけ.

questions.question: 天気予報に よると、明日は 雨だ（　　）。
questions.explanation: After だ only hearsay そうだ fits.
questions.translation: According to the weather forecast, it will rain tomorrow.
notes: ようだ follows a noun with の (雨のようだ), and it's your own guess. Hearsay is そうだ.
らしい follows a noun directly (雨らしい), not だ. Plain hearsay is 雨だ そうだ.
みたいだ follows a noun directly (雨みたいだ). Hearsay is そうだ.

questions.question: 田中さん、今日は 来ない（　　）よ。
questions.explanation: Casual quote: って.
questions.translation: Mr. Tanaka says he isn't coming today.
notes: と needs a verb like 言って いた. Ending with と よ isn't standard. Casual "he says" is って.
ので gives a reason. Passing on what he said is って.
ように is a wish or order. Passing on what he said is って.

questions.question: 「さくら」（　　）店を 知って いますか。
questions.explanation: Named: と いう N.
questions.translation: Do you know a shop called "Sakura"?
notes: といった means "such as" for examples. A name is という.
とした is "supposed". A name is という.
とは defines a word. "A shop called" is という.

questions.question: 「ありがとう」は インドネシア語で「Terima kasih」（　　）。
questions.explanation: X は Y と 言います = X is called Y.
questions.translation: "Arigatou" is "Terima kasih" in Indonesian.
notes: 話す takes the language or topic, not a quote. "X is called Y" is と 言います.
に marks a listener. A quote takes と: と 言います.
を marks an object, not a quote. Use と 言います.

questions.question: 彼は 友だち（　　）、家族の ような 存在だ。
questions.explanation: Rather than: というより.
questions.translation: He's less a friend than someone like family to me.
notes: にとって means "for (someone)". "Less a friend than family" is というより.
について means "about". Use というより.
によって means "by". A comparison of words is というより.

questions.question: 今日は すずしい（　　）、寒いくらいだ。
questions.explanation: Rather than cool, cold: というより.
questions.translation: It's not so much cool today as almost cold.
notes: にとって means "for (someone)". "More cold than cool" is というより.
によって means "by / depending". Use というより.
について means "about". Use というより.

questions.question: {泣|な}きたい（　　）悲しかった。
questions.explanation: So sad I wanted to cry: ほど.
questions.translation: I was so sad I wanted to cry.
notes: ばかり means "only". Degree (so sad that) is ほど.
しか needs a negative verb. Degree is ほど.
こそ stresses a thing. Degree is ほど.

questions.question: 信じられない（　　）きれいな 景色だった。
questions.explanation: Unbelievably beautiful: ほど.
questions.translation: The scenery was unbelievably beautiful.
notes: しか needs a negative verb. Degree is ほど.
こそ stresses a thing. "Unbelievably" is ほど.
ばかり means "only". Degree is ほど.

questions.question: 自分の 部屋（　　）自分で 掃除しなさい。
questions.explanation: At least (minimum): くらい.
questions.translation: At least clean your own room yourself.
notes: ほど shows degree. "At least (the minimum)" is くらい.
しか needs a negative verb. "At least your own room" is くらい.
ばかり means "only / nothing but". The minimum is くらい.

questions.question: 電話（　　）して くれれば よかったのに。
questions.explanation: At least a call: くらい.
questions.translation: You could at least have called me.
notes: ほど shows degree. "At least a call" is くらい.
こそ stresses a thing. The minimum is くらい.
ばかり means "only / nothing but". The minimum is くらい.

questions.question: 靴を（　　）まま、部屋に 入らないで ください。
questions.explanation: た-form + まま.
questions.translation: Please don't come into the room with your shoes on.
notes: まま needs the た-form here: はいた まま. はく まま isn't said.
The て-form can't come before まま. Use はいた まま.
The stem can't come before まま. Use はいた まま.

questions.question: めがねを かけた（　　）、おふろに 入って しまった。
questions.explanation: Still wearing glasses: た-form + まま.
questions.translation: I got into the bath with my glasses still on.
notes: かけた ばかり means "had just put on" and would need で to link. "Still wearing" is まま.
かけた ところ is "just put on". "With them still on" is まま.
うちに means "while it lasts". "Still on" is まま.

questions.question: 朝ご飯を（　　）ずに、学校へ 行った。
questions.explanation: ない-stem + ずに. (する → せずに)
questions.translation: I went to school without eating breakfast.
notes: ず follows the ない stem: 食べ + ず. 食べない ず is wrong.
The て-form doesn't take ず. Use 食べずに.
The dictionary form doesn't take ず. Use 食べずに.

questions.question: 勉強（　　）試験を 受けた。
questions.explanation: する → せずに.
questions.translation: I took the exam without studying.
notes: する becomes せず. しず is a common mistake.
ない and ず both make it negative; use only ず: せずに.
さず is the form of a verb like 出す (出さず). する becomes せず.

questions.question: 日本に（　　）以来、毎日 日本語で 日記を 書いて いる。
questions.explanation: て-form + 以来 = ever since.
questions.translation: Since coming to Japan, I've been writing a diary in Japanese every day.
notes: 以来 needs the て-form: 来て 以来.
The た-form doesn't take 以来 after a verb. Use 来て 以来.
こ is not a form that connects to 以来. Use 来て 以来.

questions.question: 大学を 卒業して（　　）、彼とは 一度も 会って いない。
questions.explanation: Since graduating (and still now): て 以来. とたん needs た-form, 最中 needs ている / の.
questions.translation: I haven't seen him even once since we graduated from university.
notes: うちに means "while it lasts". "Since then until now" is 以来.
とたん follows a た-form for one moment. "Ever since" is 以来.
最中 needs 〜て いる or N の. "Ever since" is 以来.

questions.question: 資料が でき（　　）、メールで お送りします。
questions.explanation: Stem + {次第|しだい} = as soon as, then I'll act. とたん is for something that already happened unexpectedly.
questions.translation: As soon as the documents are ready, I'll send them to you by email.
notes: とたん follows the た-form (できた とたん), and it's for an unexpected event. A promise is {次第|しだい}.
たびに follows the dictionary form and means "every time". "As soon as" is {次第|しだい}.
うちに follows 〜て いる, 〜ない or an adjective, not a stem. "As soon as" is {次第|しだい}.

questions.question: 雨が（　　）{次第|しだい}、出発しましょう。
questions.explanation: ます-stem + {次第|しだい}.
questions.translation: Let's set off as soon as the rain stops.
notes: {次第|しだい} follows the stem: やみ {次第|しだい}. Not the た-form.
{次第|しだい} follows the stem, not the dictionary form.
{次第|しだい} follows the stem, not the て-form.

questions.question: 雨が 降らない（　　）、帰りましょう。
questions.explanation: Before it starts: ない-form + うちに. 前に takes the dictionary form (降る 前に).
questions.translation: Let's go home before it starts raining.
notes: 前に follows the dictionary form (降る 前に), never 〜ない. With 降らない, use うちに.
たびに means "every time". Before it starts raining is うちに.
とたん follows a た-form. "Before it rains" is 降らない うちに.

questions.question: 忘れない（　　）、メモして おこう。
questions.explanation: Before I forget: 忘れない うちに.
questions.translation: Let me make a note before I forget.
notes: までに is a deadline and can't follow 〜ない. "Before I forget" is 忘れない うちに.
後で follows a た-form and means "after". Use うちに.
ところで means "even if" or "by the way". Use うちに.

questions.question: 病気に なって（　　）、{健康|けんこう}の 大切さが わかった。
questions.explanation: Only once I got sick did I understand: て はじめて.
questions.translation: It was only after I got sick that I understood how important health is.
notes: 以来 needs a state that continues (わかって いる). A realization at that moment is 〜て はじめて.
〜て ばかり means "only doing". "Only after I got sick" is て はじめて.
〜ても means "even if". Getting sick is what made you understand: て はじめて.

questions.question: 自分で 料理を して（　　）、母の 大変さを 知った。
questions.explanation: て はじめて. うちに, とたん and まま don't follow the て-form.
questions.translation: It was only when I cooked for myself that I realized how hard my mother had it.
notes: うちに after a て-form needs いる (して いる うちに). "Only when I did it" is して はじめて.
とたん follows a た-form. "Only after" is て はじめて.
まま follows a た-form. "Only after" is て はじめて.

meaning: for the first time in (a while)

questions.question: {久|ひさ}し（　　）に 会った 友だちは、全然 変わって いなかった。
questions.explanation: After a long time: {久|ひさ}しぶりに.
questions.translation: The friend I met after a long time hadn't changed at all.
notes: ごと is "every" (一日ごと). "After a long time" is {久|ひさ}しぶり.
おき is "every other" (一日おき). "After a long time" is ぶり.
まで is "until". "After a long time" is ぶり.

questions.question: 高校を 卒業して から、10年（　　）に クラスメートと 会った。
questions.explanation: For the first time in 10 years: 10年ぶりに.
questions.translation: I met my classmates for the first time in 10 years since we graduated from high school.
notes: ほど is "about". "For the first time in 10 years" is 10年ぶり.
ずつ is "each". Use 10年ぶり.
うち is "within". Use 10年ぶり.

meaning: as (one thing changes, so does another)

questions.question: 年を とる（　　）、体が 弱く なる。
questions.explanation: As you age: につれて (gradual change on both sides).
questions.translation: As you get older, your body gets weaker.
notes: によって means "by / depending on". Change along with age is につれて.
にとって means "for (someone)". Use につれて.
に 対して means "toward". Use につれて.

questions.question: 試験が 近づく（　　）、{緊張|きんちょう}して きた。
questions.explanation: As the exam gets closer: につれて.
questions.translation: As the exam got closer, I started to get nervous.
notes: にかけて is a time or place range (from … to). "As it gets closer" is につれて.
において means "in / at (a place)". Use につれて.
に加えて means "in addition to". Use につれて.

questions.question: 山を 登る（　　）、空気が うすく なる。
questions.explanation: As you climb: に したがって.
questions.translation: As you climb the mountain, the air gets thinner.
notes: に 関して means "about". Change along with climbing is に したがって.
に とって means "for (someone)". Use に したがって.
を 通して means "through". Use に したがって.

questions.question: 先生の 指示（　　）、{避難|ひなん}して ください。
questions.explanation: Following instructions: N に したがって.
questions.translation: Please evacuate following your teacher's instructions.
notes: に 対して means "toward". Following instructions is に したがって.
に とって means "for (someone)". Use に したがって.
に 関して means "about". Use に したがって.

questions.question: 時代の 変化（　　）、言葉も 変わって いく。
questions.explanation: Changing along with the times: と ともに.
questions.translation: Language changes along with the changing times.
notes: に 対して means "toward". Changing along with the times is と ともに.
に 関して means "about". Use と ともに.
を はじめ means "starting with". Use と ともに.

questions.question: 家族（　　）、新しい 年を 迎えた。
questions.explanation: Together with family: と ともに.
questions.translation: I welcomed the new year together with my family.
notes: に よって means "by". "Together with my family" is と ともに.
に とって means "for (someone)". Use と ともに.
を もとに means "based on". Use と ともに.

questions.question: 私（　　）、家族が いちばん 大切です。
questions.explanation: From my point of view: に とって.
questions.translation: For me, family is the most important thing.
notes: に 対して means "toward". "For me" (my view) is に とって.
に よって means "by / depending on". Use に とって.
に ついて means "about". Use に とって.

questions.question: この 問題は 子ども（　　）難しすぎる。
questions.explanation: Too hard for children: に とって.
questions.translation: This problem is too difficult for children.
notes: に ついて means "about". "Too hard for children" is に とって.
と して means "as (a role)". Use に とって.
を 通して means "through". Use に とって.

questions.question: 日本の {歴史|れきし}（　　）レポートを 書いた。
questions.explanation: A report about: に ついて.
questions.translation: I wrote a report about Japanese history.
notes: に とって means "for (someone)". A report about history is に ついて.
に よって means "by". Use に ついて.
と して means "as". Use に ついて.

questions.question: その 件（　　）は、後で 説明します。
questions.explanation: About that matter: に ついて は.
questions.translation: I'll explain that matter later.
notes: に とって means "for (someone)". "About that matter" is に ついて.
に 加えて means "in addition to". Use に ついて.
を はじめ means "starting with". Use に ついて.

questions.question: 去年（　　）、今年は 雪が 多い。
questions.explanation: Compared with last year: に {比|くら}べて.
questions.translation: Compared with last year, there's a lot of snow this year.
notes: に ついて means "about". Comparing years is に {比|くら}べて.
に とって means "for (someone)". Use に {比|くら}べて.
に よって means "by / depending on". Use に {比|くら}べて.

questions.question: 都会（　　）、いなかは 物の 値段が 安い。
questions.explanation: Compared with the city: に {比|くら}べて.
questions.translation: Compared with the city, things are cheaper in the countryside.
notes: に ついて means "about". Comparing city and countryside is に {比|くら}べて.
に とって means "for (someone)". Use に {比|くら}べて.
を はじめ means "starting with". Use に {比|くら}べて.

questions.question: 病気の 社長（　　）、部長が あいさつした。
questions.explanation: On behalf of the president: に 代わって.
questions.translation: The department manager gave the speech in place of the president, who was sick.
notes: に とって means "for (someone)". Speaking in someone's place is に 代わって.
に よって means "by / depending on". "In place of the president" is に 代わって.
に 加えて means "in addition to". The president didn't speak: に 代わって.

questions.question: 最近は 人間（　　）、ロボットが 工場で 働いて いる。
questions.explanation: Robots instead of people: に 代わって.
questions.translation: These days, robots work in factories in place of people.
notes: に とって means "for (someone)". Robots taking people's place is に 代わって.
に ついて means "about". Use に 代わって.
を 通して means "through". Use に 代わって.

questions.question: 今夜から 明日（　　）、大雨に なるでしょう。
questions.explanation: From tonight through tomorrow (loose range): から … に かけて. までに is a deadline.
questions.translation: From tonight through tomorrow, there will probably be heavy rain.
notes: までに is a deadline. A range from tonight through tomorrow is に かけて.
に わたって needs a length (3日間に わたって), not one day. Use に かけて.
に よって means "by / depending on". Use に かけて.

questions.question: 関東（　　）東北に かけて、{地震|じしん}が あった。
questions.explanation: The pair is から … に かけて.
questions.translation: There was an earthquake across the area from Kanto to Tohoku.
notes: まで already means "until". The pair is から … に かけて.
に doesn't start a range. The pair is から … に かけて.
を doesn't start a range. The pair is から … に かけて.

questions.question: 会議は 5時間（　　）続いた。
questions.explanation: Over five full hours: に わたって.
questions.translation: The meeting went on for five hours.
notes: に かけて is a range from one point to another. A length (5 hours) is に わたって.
に {比|くら}べて means "compared with". Use に わたって.
に 対して means "toward". Use に わたって.

questions.question: この 道は 10キロ（　　）、さくらが さいて いる。
questions.explanation: Along the whole 10 km: に わたって.
questions.translation: Cherry blossoms are blooming along this road for 10 kilometers.
notes: を はじめ means "starting with". A length (10 km) is に わたって.
に とって means "for (someone)". Use に わたって.
に よって means "by / depending on". Use に わたって.

questions.question: 試合は 市民 体育館（　　）行われます。
questions.explanation: Formal place: に おいて (= で).
questions.translation: The match will be held at the city gymnasium.
notes: に とって means "for (someone)". A formal place is に おいて.
に ついて means "about". Use に おいて.
に 対して means "toward". Use に おいて.

questions.question: 現代社会（　　）、インターネットは 欠かせない。
questions.explanation: In modern society: に おいて.
questions.translation: In modern society, the internet is indispensable.
notes: を もとに means "based on". "In modern society" is に おいて.
に 加えて means "in addition to". Use に おいて.
を 通して means "through". Use に おいて.

questions.question: これは 外国人（　　）に 作られた ガイドブックです。
questions.explanation: Made for a target group: 向け. 向き = happens to suit someone.
questions.translation: This is a guidebook made for foreigners.
notes: 向き means "suited to" (by nature). A guidebook made on purpose for someone is 向け.
らしく means "typical of". Made for someone is 向け.
っぽく means "-ish". Made for someone is 向け.

questions.question: {高齢者|こうれいしゃ}（　　）の サービスを 始める ことに なった。
questions.explanation: A service for older people: 向け.
questions.translation: It's been decided that we'll start a service for elderly people.
notes: っぽい means "-ish". A service made for elderly people is 向け.
だらけ means "full of". Use 向け.
がち is a bad habit. Use 向け.

questions.question: 留学（　　）、自分の 国の ことを もっと 知りたく なった。
questions.explanation: Studying abroad was the trigger: を きっかけに.
questions.translation: Studying abroad made me want to know more about my own country.
notes: に {比|くら}べて means "compared with". "Studying abroad made me want" is を きっかけに.
に 加えて means "in addition to". Use を きっかけに.
に 代わって means "in place of". Use を きっかけに.

questions.question: ある 映画を 見た ことを（　　）、日本語の 勉強を 始めた。
questions.explanation: A film started it: を きっかけに.
questions.translation: Seeing a certain film was what got me started studying Japanese.
notes: を もとに means "based on (a source)". What started it is きっかけに.
を はじめ is "starting with" in a list. What started it is きっかけに.
を 中心に means "centered on". Use きっかけに.

questions.question: 台風が 近づいて いるので、川が あふれる（　　）。
questions.explanation: Risk of something bad: おそれが ある.
questions.translation: A typhoon is approaching, so the river may overflow.
notes: つもりだ is a person's plan. A river doesn't plan. A danger is おそれが ある.
ように なる is a gradual change. A possible danger is おそれが ある.
わけが ない means "no way". The typhoon makes it likely: おそれが ある.

questions.question: この 薬は 眠く なる（　　）が あるので、運転の 前に 飲まないで ください。
questions.explanation: Possible bad effect: おそれが ある.
questions.translation: This medicine may make you sleepy, so please don't take it before driving.
notes: はずが ある is not a pattern. A possible bad effect is おそれが ある.
わけが ある means "there is a reason". A possible bad effect is おそれ.
つもりが ある is a person's plan. Medicine doesn't plan. Use おそれ.

questions.question: あんなに 練習したんだから、勝つ（　　）。
questions.correct: に 決まって いる
questions.explanation: Strong, confident guess: に 決まって いる.
questions.translation: We practiced so hard, so of course we'll win.
notes: わけが ない means "no way". After practicing so hard, it's the opposite: に 決まって いる.
はずが ない means "can't be". Use に 決まって いる.
ことは ない means "no need". "Of course we'll win" is に 決まって いる.

questions.question: こんな 時間に 電話したら、{迷惑|めいわく}に（　　）。
questions.explanation: Fixed form: に 決まって いる.
questions.translation: If you call at this hour, of course it'll be a nuisance.
notes: 違って いる means "is different / wrong". "Of course" is に 決まって いる.
決めて いる means "someone has decided". "Of course" is 決まって いる.
決まった is past "was decided". The pattern is に 決まって いる.

questions.question: あの 人に どこかで 会った（　　）。
questions.explanation: Before 気が する: ような.
questions.translation: I feel like I've met that person somewhere.
notes: 気が する takes a noun form: ような. ように can't come before 気.
そう can't follow a た-form (会った). Use ような 気が する.
らしい 気 is not a pattern. Use ような 気が する.

questions.question: 明日は 雨が 降る（　　）気が する。
questions.explanation: Feeling: dictionary form + ような 気が する.
questions.translation: I have a feeling it's going to rain tomorrow.
notes: ように can't come before 気. Use ような 気が する.
そうに can't come before 気. Use ような 気が する.
ことに can't come before 気. Use ような 気が する.

questions.question: この 仕事は 給料が いい（　　）、残業が 多い。
questions.explanation: Two sides of one thing: 一方で.
questions.translation: This job pays well, but on the other hand there's a lot of overtime.
notes: うちに means "while it lasts". "But on the other hand" is 一方で.
たびに means "every time". Use 一方で.
とたん follows a た-form for one moment. Use 一方で.

questions.question: スマホは 便利な（　　）、使いすぎると 体に 悪い。
questions.explanation: Convenient, but on the other hand: 一方で.
questions.translation: Smartphones are convenient, but on the other hand, using them too much is bad for your health.
notes: くせに criticizes a person. Two sides of a thing is 一方で.
おかげで is "thanks to". Being bad for you is the other side: 一方で.
ために means "because / for". Use 一方で.

questions.question: 一人暮らしは 自由な（　　）、さびしい ときも ある。
questions.explanation: Good side and bad side: 反面.
questions.translation: Living alone gives you freedom, but on the other hand, there are times when it's lonely.
notes: くせに criticizes a person. Two sides of living alone is 反面.
おかげで is "thanks to". Loneliness isn't good: 反面.
ために means "because". Freedom doesn't cause loneliness here: 反面.

questions.question: 彼は 優しい（　　）、きびしい ところも ある。
questions.explanation: Kind, but also strict: 反面.
questions.translation: He's kind, but on the other hand he has a strict side too.
notes: うえに adds a point in the same direction. Kind and strict are opposite sides: 反面.
ために means "because". Use 反面.
くせに criticizes "even though". Use 反面.

questions.question: 車の {免許|めんきょ}は 取った（　　）、ほとんど 運転して いない。
questions.explanation: Although I got it: ものの.
questions.translation: I got my driver's license, but I hardly ever drive.
notes: もので gives a reason. "I got it, but I hardly drive" is ものの.
ものだ ends a sentence. Before a second clause, "although" is ものの.
ものか is "as if!". Use ものの.

questions.question: 買うと 言った（　　）、まだ 買って いない。
questions.explanation: Said I'd buy it, but haven't: ものの.
questions.translation: I said I would buy it, but I still haven't bought it.
notes: うえに adds another point. Saying and not doing clash: ものの.
ばかりに is "just because" with a bad result. Use ものの.
おかげで is "thanks to". Use ものの.

questions.question: 残念（　　）、今回は 参加できません。
questions.explanation: Set phrase: 残念ながら = unfortunately.
questions.translation: Unfortunately, I can't take part this time.
notes: ほど shows degree. The set phrase "unfortunately" is 残念ながら.
だけ means "only". The set phrase is 残念ながら.
ばかり means "only". The set phrase is 残念ながら.

questions.question: 彼は {貧乏|びんぼう}（　　）も、幸せに 暮らして いる。
questions.explanation: Although poor: N ながらも. ので / ために / うえに would need な or の.
questions.translation: Even though he is poor, he lives happily.
notes: ので can't take も, and gives a reason. "Though poor" is {貧乏|びんぼう}ながらも.
ために can't take も here. "Though poor" is ながらも.
うえに adds, and can't follow a noun directly. "Though poor" is ながらも.

questions.question: この 町は さくらが 多い（　　）、「さくら町」と 呼ばれて いる。
questions.explanation: Origin of a name: ことから.
questions.translation: This town has a lot of cherry trees, which is why it's called "Sakura Town."
notes: ことには is "to my (surprise)" (おどろいた ことに). A reason for a name is ことから.
ことでも means "even with". Use ことから.
ことか is an exclamation (どんなに … ことか). Use ことから.

questions.question: ゆかが ぬれて いた（　　）、だれかが 水を こぼしたと わかった。
questions.explanation: Conclusion from a clue: ことから.
questions.translation: From the fact that the floor was wet, I knew someone had spilled water.
notes: ことに is "to my (feeling)". Judging from a fact is ことから.
ことは is a topic. Use ことから.
ことか is an exclamation. Use ことから.

questions.question: 約束した（　　）、必ず 守ります。
questions.explanation: Since I promised, I will: からには.
questions.translation: Now that I've promised, I'll definitely keep it.
notes: くせに criticizes "even though". "Now that I've promised" is からには.
わりに means "considering". Use からには.
ばかりに is "just because" with a bad result. Use からには.

questions.question: 留学する（　　）、その 国の 言葉を しっかり 勉強する べきだ。
questions.explanation: Now that you're going, you should: からには … べきだ.
questions.translation: If you're going to study abroad, you should study that country's language properly.
notes: のに is "even though". Studying abroad and studying the language go together: からには.
わりに means "considering". Use からには.
ばかりに is "just because" with a bad result. Use からには.

questions.question: 電車が 遅れた（　　）、遅刻して しまいました。
questions.explanation: Excuse: ものだから.
questions.translation: The train was late, so I ended up being late.
notes: くせに criticizes "even though". An excuse is ものだから.
わりに means "considering". Use ものだから.
のに is "even though". The train caused it: ものだから.

questions.question: あまりに おいしかった（　　）、食べすぎて しまった。
questions.explanation: Excuse, softer: もので.
questions.translation: It was so delicious that I ate too much.
notes: のに is "even though". Delicious food made you eat too much: もので.
くせに criticizes a person. Use もので.
けれど is "but". Use もので.

questions.question: 自分で 決めた（　　）、最後まで がんばりなさい。
questions.explanation: You decided it, so: のだから + advice.
questions.translation: You decided this yourself, so keep going until the end.
notes: のに is "even though". Your own choice is the reason: のだから.
くせに criticizes "even though". Use のだから.
わりに means "considering". Use のだから.

questions.question: もう 大人な（　　）、自分の ことは 自分で しなさい。
questions.explanation: You're an adult, so: な-adjective / noun + な のだから.
questions.translation: You're an adult now, so do your own things by yourself.
notes: のに is "even though". Being an adult is the reason: のだから.
ものの is "although". Use のだから.
けれど is "but", and な can't come before it. Use のだから.

questions.question: 実際に（　　）ことには、いいか 悪いか わからない。
questions.explanation: ない-form + ことには + negative result.
questions.translation: Unless you actually use it, you can't tell whether it's good or bad.
notes: ことには needs a negative here: 使わない ことには (unless). 使う is positive.
使った ことには is not the pattern. Unless is ない ことには.
The て-form doesn't connect to ことには. Use 使わない.

questions.question: お金が（　　）ことには、旅行に 行けない。
questions.explanation: Without money first, can't go: ない ことには.
questions.translation: Without money, I can't go on a trip.
notes: "Unless" needs the negative: ない ことには. ある is positive.
The pattern is ない ことには. あった is positive and past.
The て-form doesn't connect to ことには. Use ない.

questions.question: 雨の（　　）は、試合は 中止です。
questions.explanation: In case of rain: の 場合は.
questions.translation: In case of rain, the match will be cancelled.
notes: ところ is about a point in time or a place. "In case of" is 場合.
わけ means "reason". Use 場合.
せい blames a cause. Use 場合.

questions.question: カードを なくした（　　）、すぐに {連絡|れんらく}して ください。
questions.explanation: If you lose it: た 場合は.
questions.translation: If you lose your card, please contact us right away.
notes: ばかりに is "just because" with a bad result. "If you lose it" is 場合は.
わりに means "considering". Use 場合は.
くせに criticizes "even though". Use 場合は.

questions.question: たとえ 飛行機で 行った（　　）、間に合わないだろう。
questions.explanation: Even supposing: としても (pairs with たとえ).
questions.translation: Even if we went by plane, we probably wouldn't make it in time.
notes: たとえ pairs with 〜ても or としても, not としたら (a normal "if").
たとえ pairs with としても, not とすれば.
たとえ pairs with としても, not とすると.

questions.question: 失敗する（　　）、やって みたい。
questions.explanation: Even if I fail: としても.
questions.translation: Even if I fail, I want to give it a try.
notes: としたら is a normal "if". "Even if I fail, I want to try" is としても.
ところで means "even if (no use)" and follows the た-form. Use としても.
ために means "in order to". Nobody tries in order to fail. Use としても.

questions.question: 高い ものが いつも いい（　　）。安くて いい ものも ある。
wrong_options: に 決まって いる
questions.explanation: Not always true: とは 限らない (often with いつも / 必ずしも).
questions.translation: Expensive things aren't always good. There are cheap good things too.
notes: に 違いない means "surely". The next sentence shows the opposite: とは 限らない.
に 決まって いる means "of course". The next sentence shows the opposite: とは 限らない.
はずだ is an expectation. The next sentence denies it: とは 限らない.

questions.question: 日本人が みんな {敬語|けいご}が 上手だ（　　）。にがてな 人も 多い。
questions.explanation: Not necessarily: とは 限らない.
questions.translation: Not all Japanese people are good at keigo. Many find it hard.
notes: に 違いない means "surely". The next sentence says many aren't good: とは 限らない.
わけだ means "no wonder". Use とは 限らない.
ことだ gives advice. Use とは 限らない.

questions.question: この ゲームは 子ども（　　）、大人にも 人気が ある。
questions.explanation: Not limited to children: に 限らず.
questions.translation: This game is popular not only with children but with adults too.
notes: に とって means "for (someone)". "Not only children" is に 限らず.
に よって means "by / depending on". Use に 限らず.
に 関して means "about". Use に 限らず.

questions.question: 休みの 日（　　）、彼は 毎日 走って いる。
questions.explanation: Not only on days off: に 限らず.
questions.translation: He runs every day, not only on his days off.
notes: に {比|くら}べて means "compared with". "Not only on days off" is に 限らず.
に 対して means "toward". Use に 限らず.
を もとに means "based on". Use に 限らず.

questions.question: 彼女は 歌が 上手な（　　）、ダンスも うまい。
questions.explanation: Not only … but also: ばかりでなく … も.
questions.translation: She's not only a good singer but also a good dancer.
notes: ばかりに is "just because" with a bad result. "Not only … but also" is ばかりでなく.
だけに means "precisely because". Use ばかりでなく.
しか needs a negative. Use ばかりでなく.

questions.question: この 本は 子ども（　　）大人にも 読まれて いる。
questions.explanation: Not only children: ばかりでなく.
questions.translation: This book is read not only by children but by adults too.
notes: ばかりに is "just because" with a bad result. Use ばかりでなく.
しか needs a negative. Use ばかりでなく.
こそ stresses a thing. Use ばかりでなく.

questions.question: 好きな（　　）食べて ください。
questions.explanation: As much as you like: 好きな だけ.
questions.translation: Please eat as much as you like.
notes: しか needs a negative verb. "As much as you like" is だけ.
ばかり means "nothing but". Use だけ.
こそ stresses a thing. Use だけ.

questions.question: できる（　　）早く 返事を ください。
questions.explanation: As soon as possible: できるだけ.
questions.translation: Please reply as soon as you can.
notes: しか needs a negative verb. "As soon as possible" is できるだけ.
ほど is degree, and できる ほど isn't the set phrase. Use できるだけ.
こそ stresses a thing. Use できるだけ.

questions.question: 最終電車に 乗り遅れた。歩いて 帰る（　　）。
questions.explanation: No other option: しか ない.
questions.translation: I missed the last train. I have no choice but to walk home.
notes: ことは ない means "no need". Walking is the only choice: しか ない.
わけが ない means "no way". Use しか ない.
はずが ない means "can't be". Use しか ない.

questions.question: だれも 手伝って くれないなら、自分で やる（　　）。
questions.explanation: No choice: ほか ない (= しか ない).
questions.translation: If nobody will help me, I have no choice but to do it myself.
notes: ほど ない is not a pattern. "No choice but" is ほか ない.
だけ ない is not a pattern. Use ほか ない.
ばかり ない is not a pattern. Use ほか ない.

questions.question: その 映画を 見て、{泣|な}か（　　）いられなかった。
questions.explanation: Couldn't help crying: {泣|な}かずには いられなかった.
questions.translation: Watching that film, I couldn't help crying.
notes: なければ is part of "must" (なければ ならない). "Couldn't help" is ずには いられない.
なくては is part of "must". "Couldn't help" is ずには いられない.
ないと is "if not / must". "Couldn't help" is ずには いられない.

questions.question: 困って いる 人を 見ると、助け（　　）。
questions.correct: ずには いられない
questions.explanation: Fixed form: ずには いられない.
questions.translation: When I see someone in trouble, I can't help helping them.
notes: いけない doesn't follow ずには. The fixed form is ずには いられない.
The pattern must be negative: ずには いられない.
ならない doesn't follow ずには. Use いられない.

questions.question: 試験の {結果|けっか}が 心配で（　　）。
questions.explanation: Extremely worried: て しょうがない.
questions.translation: I'm terribly worried about my exam results.
notes: かまわない means "it's fine" and needs も. "Terribly worried" is 心配で しょうがない.
いられない follows 〜ずには. After 心配で, use しょうがない.
すまない means "sorry". Use しょうがない.

questions.question: 昨日 あまり 寝て いないので、眠くて（　　）。
questions.explanation: Same meaning, more formal: て 仕方が ない.
questions.translation: I didn't sleep much last night, so I'm terribly sleepy.
notes: The set phrase is negative: 仕方が ない.
仕方を する is not a phrase. Use 仕方が ない.
仕方で ない is not a phrase. Use 仕方が ない.

questions.question: この ケーキ、おいしいよ。食べて（　　）。
questions.explanation: Gentle "try it": て ごらん (to children, juniors).
questions.translation: This cake is delicious. Try some.
notes: ござる is a polite "be", not "try". Gentle "try it" is 食べて ごらん.
まいる is humble "go / come" for yourself. Inviting someone to try is ごらん.
おる is humble "be". "Try it" is ごらん.

questions.question: わからなかったら、もう 一度 自分で 考えて（　　）なさい。
questions.explanation: て ごらんなさい.
questions.translation: If you don't understand, try thinking about it once more on your own.
notes: なさい attaches to a stem: 考えて みなさい. みて なさい is wrong. Or use ごらんなさい.
いて なさい isn't a form, and it doesn't mean "try". Use ごらんなさい.
くれ is a rough "give me". It can't take なさい. Use ごらんなさい.

questions.question: 試験中は、ケータイの {電源|でんげん}を 切る（　　）。
questions.explanation: Rules and instructions end in こと.
questions.translation: During the exam, turn off your mobile phone.
